## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `dca1f17e8585b3eb953ba7928e05ac125594c575`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0139-engine-internal-semi-join-leaf-readable-parent-ids.md, docs/adr/0055-master-detail-controlled-by-parent.md + none

Read for this record: card #33820 (body, triage 6895962425, claim 6896544053, os-dev report 6896944503); ruling record 6893666857 on #33696 and the record it replaces, 6893097935, both read from the issue; PR #33992 body, file list and net diff against `main` (2 files, +43 / -0, verified on the tree); both ADRs whole at this head; `hasSuperuserReadBypass`, the cbp read filter and the engine's per-hop scope on `main` (read, not reviewed). Nothing built or run.

Check-runs on this head (46): none failed. Completed green: Check Documentation Links, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, the three `Lint · scoped` jobs, filter, Plan Test Core shards, Test UI, Dogfood Regression Gate, Auto Label. Still running when read: Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · ESLint, Type Check · workspace / source gates / consumer gates / debt ledger, Test Core (1/8). The rest are skipped by the path filter. The ADR anchor and index gates sit in the lint jobs that are still running, so their verdict is not in yet; this PASS is on the text and does not stand in for them.

### ① Derived judgments

Each rule statement the amendment makes, against the verbatim text of 6893666857:

- **Reader class — right, in all three places that state it in full** (ADR-0139 status entry, ADR-0139 D6, ADR-0055 status entry and the note under "The rules the read keeps"): view-all on the detail AND every master hop unrestricted, where unrestricted is the engine's per-hop scope and not `hasSuperuserReadBypass`, with a required master FK. The parenthesis sits where the ruling puts it, on the hop test. On `main` `hasSuperuserReadBypass` is the view-all bits on one object, so the distinction the ruling draws is real and the text keeps it.
- **What that reader gains — right.** Null and dangling-FK rows, inside its own tenant wall. Neither file says or implies the wall moves.
- **Every other reader — right.** "Every other reader, members included, keeps the chain unchanged" is carried in the ruling's words. The two near-miss readers named in D6 (unrestricted hops without view-all on the detail; view-all on the detail with a restricted hop) follow from the ruling's AND and match its reverse-pins bullet. They narrow nothing and widen nothing.
- **Tenant admins — right.** The multi-tenant bullet is quoted verbatim in ADR-0139 D6, and ADR-0055 restates it as "a master scope that is the tenant wall is not unrestricted", a faithful derivation.
- **ADR-0139 status entry — right.** Dated 2026-11-15, cites 6893666857 on #33696, names the lifted item by its quoted D6 text and by #24932 ruling B item 4 (the ruling's own identification), and says the other item stands.
- **Which D6 item is lifted — right.** D6 reads "Two things the ruling ⛔ does not take: an interim with two spellings of one scope, and 'interim removal of the predicate for an unrestricted master scope …'". The amendment lifts the second, for that class only, and says the first "stands as written". That is what the ruling orders.
- **Why ADR-0055 moves now — right, and quoted.** D6 quotes its own 2026-10-21 sentence ("ADR-0055's own text moves only in that switch's edit, never here"), says that sentence was discharged by the 2026-10-22 switch edit, and gives the ruling's order, quoted exactly, as the reason for this edit: "citing this record; ADR-0055's 10-22 note in step".
- **ADR-0055 — right.** The status entry, the mark under the 2026-10-22 entry, the §2 note and the note under "The rules the read keeps" make one statement with #30905 ruling A: an optional master's row with no master is read by its owner and by View All on the detail (unchanged); a required master has no null-master arm, and its rows with an empty or dangling reference gain exactly one reader class. "On a required master the owner has no arm" is true of the file and of the read filter on `main`. The quoted "does not open the master arm", "byte-identical" and "byte for byte" are each verbatim from the 2026-11-06 amendment.
- **Verbatim claims — right.** The three quoted bullets in D6 equal bullets 1, 2 and 5 of the record after unwrapping, bold included. The text says the record's other two bullets (pins, release note) bind the code card, which is accurate: the record has five.
- **Dates and ids — right.** 2026-11-15T11:31Z, 6893666857 replacing 6893097935, ruling B 6303721609, ruling A 2026-11-06 on #30905.

### ② Semver level

None. Docs only under `docs/adr/**`, nothing published, no changeset, label `skip-changeset`, and the Check Changeset run is green.
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

### ③ Boundary flags

- **(a) Authoring route and the thread's one wording change.** The text was authored by an os-dev subagent pinned to the tier's model inside a lower-tier thread, as the claim declares. The thread's change ("the second of the two things above that the ruling ⛔ does not take") is correct against D6, which carries one ⛔ over two items; it is more exact than "D6's ⛔" would have been. Accepted.
- **(b) Open question 1 — keep "§3 (the write gate) is not amended by this note": keep.** It is a statement about the note, it is true, and the ruling speaks only of readers. Striking it would leave a reader free to infer a write-gate change the maintainer did not rule.
- **(b) Open question 2 — which bits are view-all: no definition is owed here, and nothing is left open in ADR-0055.** ADR-0055 uses its own term, View All on the detail, which the 2026-11-06 amendment already defines (`viewAllRecords` or `modifyAllRecords`). The ruling ties its reader to ruling A, so that is the ruling's reading. If the code card lands a different bit set, that is a finding against the code, judged against this text; it is not a reason to change the amendment. Not escalated.
- **(b) Open question 3 — mark further places: not required.** The status entries and the mark under the 2026-10-22 entry govern, and "reads as of its date" is each file's own precedent. The one sentence I would still mark is N3 below.
- **(c) Amendment precedent — followed.** ADR-0139: a dated `**Amended**` status entry plus a dated D6 paragraph with a verbatim blockquote, the 2026-10-21 shape. ADR-0055: a status entry plus in-place ⚠️ notes with no end section, the 2026-10-22 shape; the mark under the 10-22 entry is on its own line because the PR is append-only, and it renders as that entry's continuation like the inline marks on the 10-26 and 11-06 entries.
- The PR is draft and Tier H: it needs a governed approver and a maintainer merge. The ruling's order (#33696's code lands only after this merges) is stated in both files.

### ④ Design judgment

**docs/adr/0139-…** True to the ruling, readable alone, and no contradiction is left standing in D6 or the status paragraph. The class, the lifted item, the untouched item and the landing order are each stated once in the status entry and once, with the verbatim bullets, in D6.

**docs/adr/0055-…** True to the ruling. The fullest statement is the note under "The rules the read keeps", which also dates the two older "unchanged" claims for a required master. The status entry reaches it by pointer.

Security judgment: the amendment states the ruling's reader class exactly and neither widens nor narrows it. No security item is raised on the code read for this review.

- S1 (should-fix) — ADR-0055 §2 note (the new line under the 2026-11-06 note) restates the class in part: it drops "inside its own tenant wall" and the "(the engine's per-hop scope, not `hasSuperuserReadBypass`)" qualifier, then says the reader "also sees the rows whose master reference is empty or dangling". §2 is the normative read section, and this is the one place a reader could take a shorter class than the ruling's. The pointer to the status line makes it recoverable, so it does not block. Either add the two phrases, or name no conditions there and only point.
- N1 (nit) — ADR-0139's status entry says "D6's other ⛔ … stands", while D6 itself (correctly, after the thread's change) speaks of one ⛔ over two things. Same meaning; the card used the same loose phrase.
- N2 (nit) — ADR-0055's mark under the 2026-10-22 entry says the class's read "carries no master predicate and no master subquery". That is the ruling's "the chain is dropped" restated as statement shape. It is true of the rule, but it is the one sentence that describes the shape of the code before the code lands; "for whom the parent chain is dropped" would say the same and age better.
- N3 (nit) — ADR-0139 D5's seventh-consumer note still says "the leaf is written on every read". After the code lands that is false for this one class. The status entry governs, so no change is owed in this PR.

No must-fix. One should-fix (S1), three nits.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-z23r42`
Reviewed-by: `session_01ADHkmRxXmVQ41fqnaTPGAv`

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `0e1c1bca51d2d6639712b356381d955883211471`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0139-engine-internal-semi-join-leaf-readable-parent-ids.md, docs/adr/0055-master-detail-controlled-by-parent.md + none

Delta record. It follows record 6896995006 (PASS on head `dca1f17e`) and judges the one commit since, `dca1f17e..0e1c1bca`. Everything in 6896995006 that this record does not restate stands on this head.

Read for this record: the commit's diff and the net diff against `main` on the tree, and the check-runs on this head. The commit touches `docs/adr/0055-master-detail-controlled-by-parent.md` only, 2 lines replaced in place; ADR-0139 is byte-identical to `dca1f17e`. The net diff against `main` is still 2 files, +43 / -0 (ADR-0139 +37, ADR-0055 +6). Nothing built or run.

Check-runs on this head (45): none failed and none cancelled. Completed green: Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, the three `Lint · scoped` jobs, Type Check · source gates, Check Documentation Links, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check PR Size, PR-body guards (the run on the push), filter, Plan Test Core shards, Test UI, Dogfood Regression Gate, Auto Label. Still running when read: Type Check · workspace, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Test Core (1/8), and a second PR-body guards run started by the body edit. Check Changeset is skipped on this head (label `skip-changeset`); the rest are skipped by the path filter. The Type Check verdicts on this head are its own: one green, three not in yet, none red.

### ① Derived judgments

Both changed lines, against the verbatim text of 6893666857:

- **ADR-0055 §2 note — right, and now the full class.** It reads: a reader who holds View All on the detail and whose every master hop answers unrestricted (the engine's per-hop scope, not `hasSuperuserReadBypass`), on a **required** master, for whom the ruling drops the parent chain, and who then sees, inside its own tenant wall, the rows whose master reference is empty or dangling; every other reader keeps the chain. The parenthesis is the ruling's, in the ruling's place, on the hop test. All three conditions are present and the tenant wall bounds the gain. Neither widened nor narrowed.
- **Mark under the 2026-10-22 entry — right.** It now reads "the parent chain over a **required** master is dropped for one reader class; every other reader is answered as this line says. See the 2026-11-15 line below." That is the ruling's own phrase, with no statement about the shape of the read. Next to the 10-22 entry it reads correctly: that entry says how the read is answered (the leaf over the master, one statement), the mark says for whom that no longer applies and where the class is defined. It names no conditions itself, so there is no shorter class to take from it.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged from 6896995006: none. Docs only, no changeset, `skip-changeset`.
Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

### ③ Boundary flags

- The commit is in-place wording on two lines this PR itself added; no line that exists on `main` is changed, so the PR is still append-only against `main`.
- Nothing else is new. The answers to the dev's three open questions in 6896995006 stand.
- Still draft and Tier H: a governed approver and a maintainer merge are owed.

### ④ Design judgment

**docs/adr/0055-…** The §2 note is now a complete statement on its own, and it agrees word for word in substance with the status entry and the note under "The rules the read keeps". No contradiction inside the file.

**docs/adr/0139-…** Unchanged; the judgment in 6896995006 stands.

Security judgment: the amendment states the ruling's reader class exactly in every place that states it, and neither widens nor narrows it.

- S1: closed. Both missing phrases are in the §2 note.
- N2: closed. The mark uses the ruling's phrase.
- N1 (nit) — open, unchanged: ADR-0139's status entry says "D6's other ⛔ … stands" where D6 has one ⛔ over two things. Same meaning.
- N3 (nit) — open, unchanged: ADR-0139 D5 still says "the leaf is written on every read". The status entry governs; nothing is owed in this PR.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:ADR-0139 状态行与 D6 各加一条 2026-11-15 修订,ADR-0055 状态行、10-22 条目下、§2 与「读取保留的规则」处各加一条注记,只追加不删改(+43/−0)。内容是你在 #33696 的裁决 6893666857「只对管理员去掉」:只有「对明细有 View All、且每一跳主对象按引擎逐跳范围都是不受限、主外键必填」的读者,父链被去掉,在自己租户墙内能看到主引用为空或悬空的行;其他读者(含成员)不变;多租户的租户管理员不算不受限。
- 为什么改:裁决原话要求「#33696 的代码 PR 必须等 ADR-0139 状态行修订(引用本记录,ADR-0055 的 10-22 注记同步)合并后才能落」。本 PR 就是这一步。
- 风险与回滚:只改决策文字,不动代码。D6 另一项禁令(同一范围两种写法的过渡)原样保留。回滚 = revert。
- 先看:ADR-0139 D6 新段(三条裁决原文引用),再看 ADR-0055 §2 新注记。
- 两分钟验证:对照 #33696 上记录 6893666857 的五条要点,读 ADR-0139 D6 引用的三条是否逐字一致。
- 需要你做的:受管面 Tier H(`docs/adr/**`)。达档(CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER)复审:首轮 6896995006(PASS,S1 should-fix),delta 6897137456 在本 head PASS、S1 已关。请批准并合并;#33696 的代码等它合并。
- 席位意见:可以合。

## 席位核对

**Verdict: ACCEPT, held for the maintainer** · head `0e1c1bca51d2d6639712b356381d955883211471` · card #33820 · report 6896944503 · at-tier contract review 6896995006 (round 1) + delta 6897137456 (PASS on this head, `S1: closed`, `N2: closed`) · read 2026-11-15T15:50Z.

- **Shape:** draft → `main`, `Fixes #33820`, `Ruling-ref: 6893666857`. `docs/adr/0139-…`, `docs/adr/0055-…`, append-only +43/−0 against `main`; `skip-changeset`. **GOVERNED**, Tier H (`docs/adr/**`). `Clause-②: no`; `Metadata-protocol: none`.
- **Premise measured:** neither ADR named 6893666857 or #33696 on `main`; #33696 is open and its code PR waits on this merge, as the ruling orders.
- **Gates:** check-runs on this head: none failing, none cancelled; the ADR lint job (docs & code guards) is green. Still running at this read: three Type Check lanes, CI/release/engine, Test Core (1/8), and the PR-body guard re-run for the body edit. The red `TypeScript Type Check` on `dca1f17e` was its lanes cancelled by the newer push, not a failure of this diff. Dev: 21 derived, 21 exit 0, `--ran` reconciles.
- **Accepted deviations:** authoring by a subagent pinned to `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` inside a lower-tier thread (recorded in the body); the thread's one wording change (which D6 item is lifted) judged right by the review. Open questions answered A in the review (keep the §3 not-amended clause; no view-all bit definition owed; no further marks). Review nits N1 and N3 accepted as written.
- **Out of scope:** none filed.
- **Landing:** Tier H. The seat does not flip this PR ready or enqueue it. It needs the maintainer's merge, or an authorised APPROVED review after which the seat lands it.
